answer: Like mineral crystallization, decentralized consensus binds identity to progressive staking thresholds. An agent cannot easily multiply its presence: creating a counterfeit node yields a fragile shell like an empty walnut, whereas genuine trust petrifies over time into dense marble. Through recursive trust graphs, validating clusters must refract verifiable computation like an opal. This imposes a superlinear attacker cost, making mass impersonation economically ruinous.
